transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. I'm Dr. [Your Name]. What brings you in today?

Well… I suppose what finally made me make the appointment is—I’ve been having these thoughts that scare me a bit. Not that I have some plan or anything like that, but I’ll think, “It would be simpler if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow.”

And then I’ll sort of tell myself not to be dramatic, you know. My sister used to say I could make a weather report sound complicated—sorry, that’s not really the point. The point is, those thoughts have been coming up, and that frightened me enough to come in.
How often have these thoughts been coming up, and when did you first start noticing them?

It’s not constant, exactly… more like it pops up, especially in those quiet moments. I first really noticed it recently, when I caught myself thinking, “It would be simpler if I just didn’t wake up tomorrow.” And then I scared myself, because I don’t have any plan to hurt myself, truly, but the thought being there at all felt… not like me.

I suppose I can’t give you a neat little calendar answer—my husband used to say I remembered recipes better than dates—but it’s been enough lately that I thought I shouldn’t just brush it off.
When did you first start experiencing these feelings and how long have they typically lasted in the past?

I think it really started about eight months ago… around when my brother’s health and, well, his behavior changed so suddenly. It sort of knocked everything sideways.

I mean, we weren’t the kind of family that had big dramatic scenes—except my aunt at Christmas, but that’s a whole other story. But yes, about eight months. It’s been hanging around since then, more or less.
Have you noticed that you don’t take pleasure in things anymore that you used to enjoy, like hobbies, time with family, or other activities?

Yes… yes, I have noticed that. I still set out my watercolor things sometimes—little jars of water, the brushes, all that—and I’ll just sit there looking at the paper.

I used to love that part, mixing colors and seeing the light change, especially in the afternoon. I took a class years ago with a woman who painted nothing but pears, which sounds dull, but they were actually beautiful… Anyway. Now I’ll sit there and the pleasure just doesn’t seem to arrive, and then I put everything away again.
Have you noticed feeling more tired or lacking energy lately, even if you’re not doing much?

I’m not sure, honestly. I mean, at my age you do sometimes sit down and think, “Well, perhaps I’m just not twenty-five anymore,” which is hardly a revelation.

I haven’t really kept track of whether it’s more than usual. Some days I’m slower getting going, but then I’ll remember I forgot to water the little fern in the kitchen and off I go fussing with that, so… I don’t know. I wouldn’t want to say for sure that it’s a big tiredness thing.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately—like trouble falling asleep or staying asleep, or on the flip side, sleeping more than usual?

Yes, sleep has been… uneven, I suppose is the word. Some nights I fall asleep all right, other nights I seem to hover just above sleep, if that makes sense.

And then I’ll wake up around three or four in the morning, which is such a miserable hour—nothing good ever gets solved at three-thirty. I start thinking about phone calls I need to return, forms I haven’t filled out properly, whether I said the wrong thing or handled something badly. It’s like my mind opens a filing cabinet in the dark.

By morning, even if I’ve technically been in bed for hours, I feel as if I’ve hardly rested.
Have you noticed yourself moving more slowly than usual, or on the contrary, feeling restless and unable to sit still?

I’m not sure I’ve noticed that exactly. I mean, I do move more slowly with certain things—getting up from the sofa, finding my glasses before I can even begin doing whatever I stood up to do—but that might just be ordinary, you know, body-being-68 sort of slowness.

Restless… I don’t think so. Not in the pacing-around way. Though I do sometimes start to straighten one drawer and end up finding old birthday cards, and then suddenly I’m reading a note from my niece from 1998, which has nothing to do with anything. So… no, I don’t think I can say I’ve clearly noticed either one.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite lately—like not feeling hungry even when it’s been a while since you last ate, or maybe losing weight without trying?

I haven’t really noticed anything clear there. My appetite sort of comes and goes, but I think it’s always done that a bit—some mornings toast sounds perfectly fine, and other mornings I make tea and then get distracted by the newspaper or the washing machine making that little thumping noise it’s been making.

I don’t think I’ve been losing weight without trying. At least, my clothes don’t seem especially different. I don’t weigh myself very often, though—scales are rather bossy objects, aren’t they? So… no, nothing definite that I’ve noticed.
Have you found it harder to do everyday tasks or focus on things you need to get done lately, like managing bills, keeping up with chores, or staying organized?

I do manage the basics, mostly. The bills get paid, the bins go out, the dishes don’t become a public health situation—though I do sometimes stand in the kitchen and forget what I went in there for, but I suppose everyone does that.

Where I’ve noticed it more is with the things that aren’t absolutely essential. I used to go with a walking group—nice women, though one of them has very strong opinions about proper footwear—and I’ve sort of stopped going. And I used to do a bit of mentoring, which I cared about, but lately I can’t seem to follow through properly. I feel like I’m there but not really there with people, if that makes sense.

So yes… I’m keeping the machinery running, but I’ve pulled back from things I used to show up for.
Have you noticed feeling down or depressed most of the day, nearly every day, for a period of at least two weeks?

Yes… I think I have, actually. Most days it feels like there’s a sort of gray film over everything. That sounds dramatic, doesn’t it, but it’s not dramatic in the moment—it’s quiet.

I’ll be making tea, or standing at the back window looking at the garden, and I know perfectly well the roses need cutting back—well, not right this second, I suppose—but there’s this heaviness sitting in me. And I try to talk myself out of it, tell myself there’s no great catastrophe happening, but it doesn’t really lift just because I’ve reasoned with it.

So yes… down, I suppose. Most days.
Have you had any distinct periods where you felt down nearly every day, and if so, how long did those periods last?

It hasn’t really been in neat little spells, if that makes sense. It’s more like it settled in and stayed.

I’d say… about eight months now. Since my brother’s health and behavior changed so suddenly. That was when I first noticed I wasn’t quite coming back up again, you know? At first I thought, well, of course I’m upset, anyone would be. And then the weeks kept going by, and the post still came, and the kettle still needed descaling—funny how kettles announce themselves at the worst times—but the low feeling was just… still there, most days.

So yes, about eight months, I think.
Have you had any distinct periods where you felt down nearly every day, lasting at least two weeks, that stand out to you as separate from the ongoing low mood you’ve described?

Not really separate, no… it all sort of blends together.

I mean, most days it’s that same gray film over everything. I can be doing something perfectly ordinary, like making tea—though I’ve become terribly particular about warming the pot first, which my daughter says is unnecessary—or just looking out at the garden, and there’s this quiet heaviness there.

It doesn’t feel like one episode that began and ended, then another one. More that it’s been sitting there in the background, and I can’t quite talk myself out of it.
Have you noticed that your movements have become noticeably slower, or that you feel unusually restless, to the point that others might have commented on it?

I’m not sure, really. I don’t think anyone’s said, “Goodness, you’re moving slowly,” or anything like that.

I do sometimes sort of potter about and then realize I’ve been standing with the cupboard open for ages—though that may just be my age, or the fact that I keep reorganizing the mugs for no good reason. My daughter bought me these blue ones that don’t stack properly, which is absurdly irritating.

But no… I can’t say I’ve noticed being obviously slowed down, or restless in a way people have commented on. At least, not that I’m aware of.
Have you noticed any significant changes in your appetite or weight recently, such as a decrease in hunger or unintentional weight loss?

I don’t think so… not in any way I’ve properly noticed.

My appetite is a bit ordinary, really. Some days I look in the fridge and nothing seems worth the bother, but then I’ll have toast or soup or something. I haven’t been keeping careful track of my weight—my bathroom scale is one of those old ones with the little needle, and I’m never sure it’s telling the truth anyway. It used to belong to my mother, actually, and she was forever tapping it with her foot before getting on, as if that would make it behave.

But no, I haven’t noticed any big weight loss or anything like that. Not that I’m aware of.

Have you had any times in the past when your mood was low enough that you felt like you needed help or that it was really affecting your life, before this current period that started about eight months ago?

I’m not sure I can think of a time like that before this, no.

I mean, I’ve had ordinary low patches over the years—everyone does, don’t they? After Christmas sometimes, or when the weather goes on being damp for weeks and the garden turns to mud. I remember one February I got terribly fed up because the boiler kept making that clanking noise and the man who came to fix it tracked dirt all through the hallway carpet.

But in terms of it really affecting my life to the point I thought I needed help… I don’t know. Nothing clear comes to mind before these last months.
